description:
Create or replace pages, each sent whole, and delete others; optionally rename the site, change its theme, or set its header, replaced whole. A page you do not send is left as it is. Every write can be undone (history, undo). The input schema gives every block's fields.

Pages
- path "" is the home page and must exist. Other paths are lowercase slugs, slash-separated, no leading slash.
- navOrder places a page in the header nav (0 first); null keeps it out. The home page is reached by the site name, so give it null.
- path "search" is the site's search results page, which every site has; no page takes it.
- path "_footer" is not a page to visit but the footer shown under every page: addresses, hours, contact details. Content and columns blocks, no hero and no h1, navOrder null. A site without one has no footer.
- description is the page's search snippet: one sentence, under 160 characters.
- Omit the id of a block you add, and keep every id a page was read with, so a wiki page's history matches its blocks one for one.

Blocks
- A page is a list of blocks, stacked vertically. Every page has exactly one h1: an opening hero's heading, a product's or a products list's with a menu, or else an h1 at the top of its first content block.
- "hero" is a heading, a sentence or two of plain text, and optionally one button. It opens a page, its heading the h1: use one on the home page and on pages that sell something. With "call": true it is a call to action further down instead, its heading an h2: at most one on a page, usually last, asking for one action, with a button. Its heading and text are plain text that may wrap words in <strong> or <em>, as the source sets them bold or italic, and its text may link words with <a href>, as the source links them; words in <strong> in its heading are also drawn in the accent colour. Its optional image is a picture filling it behind the words, by https URL, under the same rule as a pictures block. Where its words are a subheading rather than a sentence (a line or two, often set as headings at the source), give "subheading": true. With no picture, "backdrop": "mesh", "grain", "flow" or "marble" sets a slowly moving field of the site's own colours behind the words, smooth, grainy, folding like poured paint, or hard-edged as marbled paper, and "backdropSpeed" and "backdropIntensity", each 0 to 1, set how fast it moves (0.25 unset) and how strongly it folds (0.5 unset): at most one on a site, on the home page's opening, for a brief that wants a modern or striking look, and never on a site moved across from elsewhere. Over a picture or backdrop its words sit on boxes of the page's background; "box": "panel" or "accent" sets them on that colour instead, and "none" sets light words on the picture itself.
- "content" holds HTML, plain and semantic: h1–h4, p, ul, ol, li, a, strong, em, blockquote, table, hr. No class, style or script: they are stripped. No img either: a picture goes in a pictures block. After a hero, headings start at h2.
- "columns" sets 2–4 columns side by side, each {"blocks": [...]} of the blocks a column may hold (content, pictures, figures, code, link groups, references, notices, lists): for features, services or contact details. They stack on a phone. To place them freely instead, as a page builder's grid does, give every column an "area": {"col", "span", "row", "rows"} on twelve columns, rows counted from 1 (up to 12 columns then); cells may sit lower than their neighbours or overlap. With "beside": true and one column, it is a facts panel beside the text instead: on a page about one thing (a product, a place, an organisation), placed before the page's content, its usual content a picture and a two-column table of facts.
- "pictures" shows pictures by https URL, {"items": [{"src", "alt": what it shows, "caption"?}]}: one is a figure, several a row the visitor scrolls sideways. A video file is an item with "video": true, its src an MP4, and "poster"?: the picture it shows before it plays. Use only picture and video URLs the brief gives you; never invent one. For any gallery or slideshow on a site being moved across, one pictures block holding each picture once, in order, without the slideshow's counters ("Image 1 of 12") or its thumbnails. A YouTube link is an iframe in a content block.
- "product" makes its page one thing for sale: {"images": [https URLs, the first on every listing], "price"?: as it reads ("£2,500"), "sold"?: true, "tags": [the lists it appears in], "text": HTML of what it is (materials, size, year, words about it)}. It draws the page's title as the h1, so the page has no hero; it goes first. One product per page. Write a price as an amount, "£2,500", "$40" or "€12.50", and the product can be bought online once the site takes payment; "from £40" or "POA" keeps it to the Enquire button. Where it is sold elsewhere, as a book is by its publisher, give it "action": {"label": "Buy from Salmon Poetry", "href": the page that sells it}. A service, booked rather than sold (a lesson, a treatment, a consultation), is a product with "service": true, "duration"?: how long it takes as it reads ("1 hour"), and "unit"?: what its price is for as it reads after it ("an hour", "per person"); its button reads Book, and where it is booked elsewhere, "action" goes to that calendar. "sold" on a service means fully booked.
- "list" lists pages of the site, read as the page is: {"source": "under", "under"?: a path} the pages directly under it, a section's index page; {"source": "newest", "count"?, "under"?} the most recently changed, a blog's latest posts; {"source": "chosen", "pages": [paths]} those, in order; or {"source": "products", "tag"?} the product and service pages with that tag, or all, newest first. "show": "cards" (the default) draws each page's first picture, title and search snippet, "links" each title with how long ago it changed; products are always cards of their pictures, name and price, cropped square, "shape": "portrait" upright for books and posters, "landscape" wide. A shop with several lists gives each list's products block a "menu" of links to all of them, [{"label": "All", "href": "/shop"}, …], shown down the left; the block then heads the page with its title, so the page needs no other h1. A list is drawn from each page, so never copy a product's pictures, name or price onto another page; list it.
- "donate" takes gifts for a charity or a cause: {"amounts": the suggested gifts in one currency, as they read (["£10", "£20"]), "monthly"?: true where donors may give every month as well as once}. The donor may always give an amount of their own. It shows once the site takes payment. Use it only where the brief asks for donations, with the words that ask for them before it.
- "stats" sets 1–12 figures in a row, each {"value": as it reads ("1987", "40+"), "label": what it counts}: years open, customers served, awards. Only figures the brief gives.
- "testimonial" is one person's words about the business: {"quote": their words exactly, "author": their name, "role"?, "avatarUrl"?: their photo by https URL}. Only quotes the brief gives, never one written for them.
- "poem" sets one poem, or a song's words, line for line as written: {"title"?, "text": plain text, a line to a line, a blank line between stanzas, the spaces that indent a line kept, and words set in italic or bold wrapped in <em> or <strong>, "note"?: one line under it, such as where it first appeared}. Verse goes in a poem block, never a content block, whose paragraphs would run its lines together. Copy every word, line break and indent exactly, and only poems you were given.
- "codeTabs" shows code to copy in tabs, {"tabs": [{"label": "JavaScript", "language"?: "javascript", "code": "…"}]}: for a developer or a product with an API.
- "linkGrid" sets groups of links under a heading each, {"intro"?, "groups": [{"heading", "description"?, "links": [{"label", "href"}]}]}: a page of resources, or the places to go next.
- "references" lists the sources a page's claims rest on, {"title"?, "items": [{"text": the citation as HTML, "url"?}]}: at the foot of a page that cites them.
- "banner" is a notice at the top of a page about the page itself, {"variant": "stub" | "unsourced" | "outdated" | "promotional" | "cleanup" | "coi", "text"?: words in place of the standard notice}: on a wiki, where a page needs work.
- "contents" lists links to the page's own sections, its h2s. Use it at the top of a long page with several sections.
- "comments" lets visitors comment on the page, each comment shown once an owner approves it. Use it only where the brief asks for comments, usually at the foot of a blog post.
- "contact" is a form for a visitor's name, email address and message, which reaches the site's owners privately and never shows on the site. Use it on a contact page, and wherever the brief asks to be written to but gives no address to publish.
- "search" is a box that searches the site's pages as a visitor types; Enter opens the site's search page, /search, with every page that matches. Use it on a site of many pages, on the home page or a page of its own.
- Any block of the page's own (not one inside columns) may take "band": "panel" or "accent", which sets it on a strip of that colour from edge to edge. Use bands sparingly, to set a section apart; consecutive blocks with the same band read as one section.
- A button's href is a page on the site ("/contact"), an https URL, a mailto: or a tel: address. Link between pages with root-relative hrefs, never the full domain.
- Write every phone number as a tel: link and every email address as a mailto: link, so a visitor on a phone can tap it.

Theme
- Each value is a CSS colour, OKLCH preferred, e.g. "oklch(0.72 0.16 40)". Choose what suits the business, and keep text readable on bg (contrast 4.5:1 or better) and muted text still legible.
- --font-sans is one of these values, written exactly: Clean: "ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif"; Friendly: "ui-rounded, SF Pro Rounded, Nunito, Varela Round, system-ui, sans-serif"; Humanist: "Optima, Candara, Seravek, Gill Sans Nova, Noto Sans, sans-serif"; Classic: "Charter, Bitstream Charter, Sitka Text, Cambria, Georgia, serif"; Elegant: "Iowan Old Style, Palatino Linotype, Palatino, URW Palladio L, serif"; Typewriter: "ui-monospace, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace"; Inter: "var(--font-inter), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif"; Geist: "var(--font-geist), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif"; DM Sans: "var(--font-dm-sans), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif"; Manrope: "var(--font-manrope), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif"; Nunito: "var(--font-nunito), ui-rounded, system-ui, sans-serif"; Work Sans: "var(--font-work-sans), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif"; Space Grotesk: "var(--font-space-grotesk), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif"; Bricolage Grotesque: "var(--font-bricolage), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif"; Lora: "var(--font-lora), Georgia, serif"; Playfair Display: "var(--font-playfair), Georgia, serif"; Instrument Serif: "var(--font-instrument-serif), Georgia, serif"; Source Serif: "var(--font-source-serif), Georgia, serif"; Crimson Pro: "var(--font-crimson), Georgia, serif"; Bitter: "var(--font-bitter), Rockwell, Georgia, serif"; Young Serif: "var(--font-young-serif), Georgia, serif"; JetBrains Mono: "var(--font-jetbrains), ui-monospace, monospace". The first six use fonts every device has; the rest are web fonts miow serves. Nothing else loads, and a value with quotes is discarded.
- roundness, density, scale and depth are numbers from 0 to 1 that shape every page: corners from square to round, spacing from roomy to compact, headings from close to body size to far larger, and shadow from flat to raised. Choose them for the business as you choose its colours; 0.33, 0.5, 0.5 and 0 is a plain, even look.
- --hero-entrance makes an opening's words arrive as the page opens: "rise", "focus" or "unveil". Leave it unset unless the business suits motion.
- Looks to start from, each its colours in words and the rest of its theme. Where one suits the business, take its theme whole and choose colours that match its words, in the business's own hue:

Copy
- Most visitors read on a phone. Short paragraphs, plain words, the important thing first.
- Write in the business's own voice, from what you were given.
- Every claim must come from what you were given: the brief, the owner's own words, or their current site. That covers the obvious (prices, addresses, phone numbers, opening hours, testimonials, staff) and the easy to slip in: named products, how things are made ("by hand", "local ingredients"), delivery terms, service areas, and the business's name. Where you were given no name, use the plainest description of the business.
- A thin brief makes a short site. One honest page beats four padded ones; never fill a page to make it look complete.

Images: upload_image first, then use the URL it returns.

description.description: Search snippet: one sentence under 160 characters

navOrder.description: Position in the header nav, 0 first; null keeps it out

path.description: "" is the home page; else slash-separated slugs, no leading slash, never "search" or "mcp"

summary.description: What this change does, in a few words, for the history

theme.description: Keys to change. hue, chroma, tone and contrast, sent together, derive all six colours and replace those set before; a colour sent beside them is kept over it.

--button-padding.description: Space inside every button, top and bottom then the sides, "2rem 3rem"; unset, from the shape

--button-radius.description: Every button's corners as CSS border-radius, "45px 0" for a petal, "0" square, "999px" a pill; unset, from roundness

--color-header-button.description: The header button's colour; unset, the accent

--color-header-button-text.description: The colour of its words; unset, the background's

--color-heading.description: The colour of headings, the site's name and its menu; unset, they take the text's

--color-name.description: The name's colour; unset, the headings'

--color-name-strong.description: The colour of the words in <strong> in the header's styledName; unset, the name's

--color-nav.description: The menu's colour; unset, the headings'

--color-tagline.description: The line's colour; unset, the quiet text's

--color-tagline-strong.description: The colour of the words in <strong> in the line; unset, the line's

--font-header.description: The font of the site's name and its menu; unset, the headings'

--font-header-button.description: The font of the header's button; unset, the text's

--font-heading.description: Headings, and the site's name and menu unless --font-header sets theirs; unset, they take --font-sans

--font-heading-weight.description: Their weight, "700" bold; unset, each heading keeps its own

--font-name.description: The site's name in a font of its own, written as --font-sans is; unset, --font-header's

--font-nav.description: The header menu's font, written as --font-sans is; unset, --font-header's

--header-button-size.description: The size of the words on the header's button, "1.1rem"; unset, the text's

--header-padding.description: With "wide", the space above and below the header's contents, "1cqi"; unset, 2cqi

--heading-align.description: Where the headings in a page's text sit: "center" centred; unset, at the start of the line

--heading-tracking.description: Space between the letters of headings, "-0.03em" tight for a large sans; unset, the font's own

--hero-entrance.description: How an opening's heading, words and button arrive as the page opens: "rise", "focus" or "unveil"; unset or "", at once. A visitor who asks for less motion sees them at once

--hero-size.description: The size of an opening's heading on a laptop, "3rem"; unset, it grows with the window

--logo-size.description: The height of the logo in the header, "5rem"; unset, 3rem

--name-size.description: The size of the site's name in the header on a laptop, "1.8rem"; unset, the text's

--name-weight.description: The name's weight; unset, the headings'

--nav-size.description: The size of the header menu on a laptop, "1.2rem"; unset, the text's

--nav-weight.description: The menu's weight; unset, the headings'

--page-margin.description: With "wide", the margin either side of the header and pages, "4cqi" for 4% of the width; unset, 3cqi

--page-width.description: With the header's "wide", how wide pages may grow, "93.75rem"; unset, 112.5rem

--tagline-size.description: The size of the line under the name, "0.9rem"; unset, a little under the text's

--tagline-style.description: "italic" sets the line under the name in italic

--text-size.description: The size of body text on a laptop, every heading reckoned from it, "1.2rem"; unset, 1rem

adobeFonts.description: The id of the site's own Adobe Fonts web project, from its embed code use.typekit.net/<id>.css; "" removes it

chroma.description: How colourful the accent is; the rest is tinted with it faintly

contrast.description: How far text and lines stand from the background

density.description: Space between and around blocks: 0 roomy, 1 compact

depth.description: Shadow under buttons and panels: 0 flat, 1 raised

hue.description: The accent colour, as an OKLCH hue in degrees

roundness.description: Corners of buttons, pictures and panels: 0 square, 1 round

scale.description: Headings against body text: 0 close in size, 1 far larger

tone.description: 0 a dark site, 1 a light one

token.description: The site token from create_site or the site's settings. Omit if your Authorization header carries it.
